_doc: Search Console findings, 16-month export. Audit evidence, separate from the Part 6A demand signal derived from the same file.

findings.finding: 48% of the site has never been shown once in 16 months.
findings.detail: 149 of 287 URLs recorded any impression at all. 138 URLs — including most of the 150-page city x service lattice — have never appeared in a search result over the entire retention window. That is the measured form of the scaled-content problem: pages that exist, are indexable, and do nothing.

findings.finding: The homepage is effectively the whole site.
findings.detail: The homepage took 28007 of 63096 page impressions (44%) and 865 of 929 clicks (93%). Every other URL on the domain combined produces about a fifth of the traffic. A 287-page site performing as a one-page site is the clearest possible evidence that the hub-and-spoke architecture never existed.

findings.finding: Two service hubs carry large impression volume at unusable positions.
findings.detail: /roof-cleaning/ — 5,125 impressions, average position 53.5, 3 clicks. /gutter-cleaning/ — 4,781 impressions, position 57.5, 0 clicks. /commercial-window-cleaning/ — 2,300 impressions, position 58.9, 0 clicks. Google is showing these pages for thousands of queries and ranking them on page five or six. That is not a demand problem; it is a relevance and authority problem on pages that already have an audience waiting.

findings.finding: Cannibalization is confirmed in the data, not just in the crawl.
findings.detail: /services/pressure-washing/ (1,420 impressions, position 32.2) and /pressure-washing/ (356 impressions, position 43.2) are both live and both accruing impressions for the same intent. The Bellingham window-cleaning cluster behaves the same way across several URLs. The 197-row redirect map already consolidates these; this is the measurement that justifies it.

findings.finding: Click-through rate collapses at ranks that should convert.
findings.detail: 'window cleaning bellingham' sits at position 9.4 with 2,194 impressions and 28 clicks — 1.3%. Position 9-10 on a local commercial term should do several times that. Sitewide the desktop CTR is 0.86% against mobile's 4.7%, on nearly twice the desktop impressions. Titles and descriptions are leaving clicks on the table at ranks already earned.

findings.finding: House washing has almost no query demand under that name.
findings.detail: 71 impressions across 6 queries in 16 months, against 15,850 for window cleaning and 4,910 for gutters. 'Soft wash' and 'siding' return almost nothing either. The service is real and worth selling; the evidence says it is not a head term in this market and should hang off the pressure-washing and roof clusters rather than carry its own demand expectation.

findings.finding: Striking distance is one market and one service.
findings.detail: 32 queries sit at positions 8-20 with 50 or more impressions. Nearly all are Bellingham, and most are window cleaning variants. The fastest available wins are not new pages in new towns — they are the Bellingham head terms already on the edge of page one.

geo_lattice_verdict.verdict: The 150-page city x service lattice produced 388 impressions and 1 clicks in 16 months — 0.6% of the site's impressions and 0.1% of its clicks, at a median position of 41.0. 88 of the 150 were never shown at all. This is the v1 lattice pattern doing exactly what Keystone v2 Part 6A was written to prevent: pages generated from a towns array rather than from evidence, indexed, and invisible.
